Maya — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick read: we can support the steady-state and planned bursts, but want to align on two pieces before we finalize the SOW: pricing for committed reserve + transient burst crediting, and an operational fallback for short-notice surges.

High-level proposal: 
- Reserved slab: compute capacity sized to cover steady throughput (120 sessions), configured as a Dedicated pool pinned to US-West.
- Shoulder headroom: a reserved shoulder buffer equivalent to ~30% of steady to absorb frequent small spikes without invoking burst.
- Burst policy: allow ephemeral burst up to 2.5x of steady for short windows (policy gates per-customer and per-pool). Bursts beyond reserved shoulder will draw from a shared transient pool (opportunistic GPUs) with pre-negotiated eviction priority.
- Fallback: when transient pool unavailable, route excess requests to a quantized lower-cost model family (r12-q4) with graceful knob-controlled quality degradation; include circuit-breaker and graceful 429/503 policy.

Action items I propose:
1) Karthik to outline the autoscale knobs and expected latency delta for quantized fallback.
2) Monica to propose commercial terms (burst credits, overage cadence).
3) Aditya to confirm VPC + region constraints and any CA/contract notes for Private timeline.

I'll draft a one-pager we can share with Procurement.

— Jonas

Thanks — dug into the numbers in the spreadsheet. Short technical notes and recommended policy primitives: 

1) Sizing rationale
- Baseline capacity: estimate ~4x A100-80GB equivalent per 100 concurrent sessions at 900-token average (includes headroom for KV cache). For 120 sessions ~5 CPUs equivalent should be allocated; I'll convert to exact GPU counts after validating sequence length distribution.
- Shoulder buffer: 30% (conservative) -> add ~2 additional A100-eq GPUs nominally assigned to the customer but preemptible for higher-priority traffic.

2) Autoscale policy (recommended default)
- Scale trigger: sustained 60s average > 70% GPU utilization -> scale by 1 GPU unit.
- Burst window cap: max of +2 GPUs or +2.5x baseline for windows < 6 hours (whichever limits first).
- Cooldown policy: 10m steady under 50% utilization to scale down.
- Eviction priority: Dedicated reserved > shoulder buffer > transient shared pool. Short-lived ephemeral jobs will be preempted first.

3) Fallback model plan
- Primary model: r14 (FP16/8-bit path) for P95 latency target.
- Fallback: r12-q4 with smaller KV cache footprint — expect ~1.6x latency at P95 but ~50% cost reduction. Route via routing policy with greylist to minimize user-visible regressions.

4) Observability & SLOs
- Token-level latency, model-switch events, and eviction traces exposed to Console. Alert on model-switch > 2 events per day.

Attachments: autoscale_policy_matrix.csv (matrix of triggers / scale increments)

Happy to run a quick sizing demo with your infra lead — ping with times.

— Karthik
